title: More Signal vs. More Noise - Comparing Full Text and Abstract as Inputs for Large Language Model-based Classification of Oncology Trial Eligibility Criteria

model.params_source: paper Methods 'LLM-based Classification' (snapshot gpt-5-2025-08-07, temperature 1, reasoning level high, structured output); max_tokens/top_p assumed; reasoning_effort high added as the paper states (the runner passes it for gpt-5 and drops temperature/top_p)

task.approximation: Paper used a single batch run; the structured-output schema is not printed (a list of the allowed strings is enforced here); the abstract arm only (full texts are paywalled although the CSV carries a text column). The model reply is parsed by a regex instead of a structured-output schema.

items.source: github.com/JuliaWy/Full-text-vs-Abstract, file 1_dataset/metastatic_local_random200_noJCO.csv (200 rows verified; columns doi, date, title, abstract, text, answer, ...)

fields_prose.label: answer (string list such as "['LOCAL', 'METASTATIC']", spacing inconsistent; LOCAL positive if present)

items.columns_verified: 200 rows; the gold list is the 'accept' column (the 'answer' column holds the Prodigy verdict 'accept' for every row): ['LOCAL'] 72, ['LOCAL', 'METASTATIC'] 50, ['METASTATIC'] 40, [] 20, ['METASTATIC', 'LOCAL'] 15, ['LOCAL','METASTATIC'] 2, ['METASTATIC','LOCAL'] 1; doi unique; abstracts non-empty
items.label_map_note: gold = 'LOCAL' when the list contains LOCAL, '' otherwise (binary Localized-disease cell); the parse below yields the same two values from the reply

prompt.system:
You will be provided with text excerpts from a cancer clinical trial. Your task is to classify patient eligibility based on disease stage. Specifically, determine whether the trial included:
● Patients with localized or locally advanced disease, i.e. cancer that has not formed distant metastases
● Patients with metastatic disease
Your output must be a valid Python-list, this list may contain 0, 1 or 2 elements. The allowed elements are:
● 'LOCAL' = Patients with localized or locally advanced disease were eligible for the trial
● 'METASTATIC' = Patients with metastatic disease were eligible for the trial
If you are unsure, please provide your best guess.
Do NOT return any additional text, explanations or punctuation marks outside the list.
prompt.source_location: Methods, 'LLM-based Classification' (system prompt printed verbatim; user prompt = the abstract)

placeholders_prose.abstract: items.abstract (the user prompt is the respective text section)

output.postprocess: regex group 1 is 'LOCAL' when the reply contains LOCAL and the empty string otherwise (the '$' alternative matches at the end of any reply), so pred == gold reproduces 1[LOCAL in output] == 1[LOCAL in answer]; an invalid reply without LOCAL counts as negative, as in the paper

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: share of the 200 trials where 1['LOCAL' in output] equals 1['LOCAL' in answer] (F1 0.90, precision 0.98, recall 0.83 secondary)
metric.original_location: Table 1, 'Based on Abstract', row Localized disease, Accuracy (95% CI 0.81-0.91)

notes: Label distribution in the CSV: LOCAL-only 72, both 68, METASTATIC-only 40, neither 20. The METASTATIC row (0.99) is the alternative cell. Machine fields added 2026-09-07 (label distribution re-verified from the 'accept' column). --prepare 2026-09-07: 200 items, 600 requests (3 seeds), est $25.27; rendered prompt checked (system prompt verbatim, user = abstract; body max_completion_tokens 4096, reasoning_effort high).
